title: fullcycle has no restore half, so it is permanently red on dev-profile estates
body:
## Summary

**`fullcycle` has no restore half, so on any estate whose `build all` is dev-profile it is now guaranteed to finish red on every invocation.**

Confirmed live in Conflab by `conflab/vc`, 2026-09-01. hv re-ran the cycle at 19:03Z with all four PATH links resolving beforehand:

    clean rust  rc=0
    build all   rc=0
    test rust   rc=0
    THIS CYCLE DARKENED BINARIES IT DID NOT RESTORE
    4 link(s) resolved before this run and do not now
    FULLCYCLE FINISHED -- rc=1

**The check is correct and the red is true.** `build all` there is the devbin builtin at the dev profile -- no `build-rust` script, no `build.` override in that project's config -- so every run deletes `release/`, rebuilds `debug/`, and correctly reports damage.

## Why a true red is still a bad steady state

**A gate that is red in the ordinary case teaches people to ignore it.** hv's first reaction to the red was *"this seems bad"*, which is exactly the reading a permanently-failing gate trains.

This is the same argument that killed the `> 1 declared test target is a breach` rule earlier the same day -- **with one difference that matters: that rule was red on a CORRECT configuration, and this is red on a genuinely broken one.** So the answer is not to soften the check. The cycle is missing its restore half.

`_fullcycle_can_rebuild` is still the `build --help` proxy, unchanged. **The after-check has made the proxy harmless rather than made it true**, which is a defensible place to stand but should be stood in knowingly.

## Three options, not equivalent

1. **A restore phase after `build all`** -- rebuild release for anything the snapshot is watching. Targeted: costs a release build only on estates that actually have PATH links into the tree, and makes the cycle net-non-destructive, **which is what the FAIL CLOSED comment already claims it is**.
2. **`build all` builds release too.** Simple, and taxes every fullcycle on every estate with a full optimised build whether or not anything depends on `release/`. In Conflab the two release builds took 1m09s and 1m05s against a 6m52s debug-plus-Xcode phase.
3. **Leave it; let the red stand as the instruction.** Honest, and it makes the verb unusable as a gate on that estate.

`conflab/vc` recommends **1**, on the grounds that it is the only option under which `_fullcycle_can_rebuild`'s promise becomes true rather than approximately true.

**Not decided here.** `fullcycle` is destructive by design and this changes what it does, on eleven estates. hv's call.

## Related

`0048` is the same weakness from the other side: where no PATH link exists, the check cannot fire at all and the cycle goes green having measured nothing. **Here the tripwire exists and fires correctly; there it is absent and silent.** Option 1 would fix this issue and leave `0048` open.

## A second finding recorded with it

`conflab/vc`'s own earlier at-risk census named three directories by hand -- `~/.local/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` -- found two dangling links and reported them restored. **There are four**: `~/bin` carries a second pair pointing at the same two targets. Their fix happened to be complete because four links resolve through two binaries; their enumeration was not, and nothing in the output said which directories it had covered.

`fullcycle` enumerates PATH rather than a hand-listed set, which is why it saw all four. **Same class as the day's recurring defect -- a sound instrument with a population one unit too narrow -- caught this time by the tool rather than by a person.**
